sections.h2: Prince George's County at a glance
sections.html:
Prince George's County sits on the eastern side of Washington, D.C. The county seat is Upper Marlboro. The 2020 census counted 967,201 people, and the 2025 estimate is 970,374, which puts it second in Maryland by population.

Federal jobs shape the local market. Joint Base Andrews, NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, the Internal Revenue Service and the U.S. Census Bureau are all major employers, so a reassignment can force a sale on a short clock. Buyers often start by measuring the walk or drive to one of the county's 15 Metro stations or its MARC stops.

Geography shows up on the bill. A house inside an incorporated city, such as Bowie, carries a municipal tax and gets a reduced county rate, while a house on unincorporated land pays the county rate in full. Check which one applies before you read a bill.

Each July the county sends bills, with full payment due September 30. Late payments add interest and a penalty, and not getting the bill is no defense. Tax years run from July 1 through June 30.

If the bill is marked Principal Residence, you may pay half by September 30 and half by December 31, though Maryland allows a service charge of up to 1.65% on the second half. Late charges are listed at 1.67% per month in the county's Tax Facts guide, so paying on time is worth it.

sections.h2: What rates make up a bill
sections.html:
Several separate rates stack up on one bill, each quoted for every $100 of assessed value. Here are the fiscal 2026 figures.

ChargeRate per $100 of assessed value
County$1.0000 (reduced in incorporated areas)
State$0.1120
M-NCPPC (Park and Planning)$0.2940
Washington Suburban Transit Commission$0.0260
Stormwater and flood control$0.0540 (Area 1), $0.0120 (Area 2)

The formula is simple: divide the assessment by 100, multiply by the rate, then add any extra charges.

Extra charges can appear on the same bill. Front Foot Benefit pays for sewer or water mains laid in the street; WSSC at 301-206-8032 handles questions. Solid Waste Service pays for trash and waste programs (Department of the Environment, 301-952-7630). A tax lien charge appears when taxes or fines are in arrears.

Values come from the State Department of Assessments and Taxation, which looks at each property every three years. Residential values rose 10.3% in the January 1, 2026 cycle compared with January 1, 2023, with notices mailed December 30, 2025. A higher value is spread in equal steps over three years; a lower one applies in full for the 2026 tax year.

The Homestead and Homeowners' credits are run by the state, and the county lists its own credits on its Property Tax Credits page.

How to appeal your assessment

Disagreements start with the state assessments department, then go to the county Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board, then to the Maryland Tax Court. For a dwelling, the appeal board must hold a hearing within 120 days after receiving the request, unless the owner asks for a delay.

For questions, call Treasury Customer Service at 301-952-4030 on weekdays between 9:00 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. The counter is in the Wayne K. Curry Administration Building, 1301 McCormick Drive, Suite 1100, Largo.

  • Online, through the Tax Inquiry site. An e-check costs $1.50, a Visa debit card $3.95 and other cards 2.45%.
  • By phone at 855-516-1830, with added fees.
  • By mail, with the bill stub, to P.O. Box 37050, New York, NY 10087.
  • At the Largo counter from 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. The counter does not take cash.
  • Day or night, a walk-up slot at the front entrance accepts checks, money orders and cashier's checks. A drive-up drop box opens at the end of September and December.

Email questions go to tax_inquiry@co.pg.md.us. When a house is being sold, the title company usually pays the bill from proceeds, so the seller only needs the current account balance.

On the second Monday in May the county auctions any real property tax still unpaid, and the highest bidder gets the lien. A late bill becomes a debt held by a stranger, so treat that date as firm.

A conventional listing can be hard when taxes are behind, because lenders and title companies want the balance cleared at closing. Some cash buyers will pay the arrears out of the price at settlement. Before you choose a closing date, get a payoff from the Treasury Division that includes any tax lien charge.

Sales trigger transfer and recordation taxes, and each county sets its own. For Prince George's, a 2026 General Assembly staff table shows a 1.4% transfer tax and recordation tax of $2.75 per $500 of consideration. Neither changed from fiscal 2022 through fiscal 2027. The state adds its own 0.5% transfer tax on top of the local rate.

The contract of sale decides which side pays and how the split is written. Confirm the exact amounts with the title company, since municipal and state add-ons differ by deal.

The county's Office of Homeland Security code compliance staff enforce housing, zoning and rental rules. Inspectors act on complaints or cleanup sweeps and issue a Notice of Violation, a Civil Citation or both, with a deadline to fix the problem.

  • To report a violation, call 311 within the county or 301-883-4748 from outside it, weekdays from 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m.
  • A single-family rental needs a county license, valid for two years, unless the city or town licenses it instead. Bowie is among the municipalities the county does not license.
  • A license is refused when an inspector finds life-safety violations, including unpermitted construction or an illegal conversion.
  • Landlords who use a pre- or post-settlement occupancy agreement between buyer and seller are exempt from the license requirement.

A house with open citations or unpermitted work can lose bids, so a seller who cannot fix them in time may prefer an as-is sale.

Maryland Real Property Code section 10-702 requires the seller of a home with one to four units to hand the buyer either a disclosure or a disclaimer statement by the time the contract is signed. The disclaimer says the home is sold as-is, except for known latent defects.

Exemptions cover bank sales after foreclosure, sheriff and tax sales, and fiduciary transfers in estates and trusts. A buyer who gets the statement late can back out within five days of receiving it, and no contract term can take that right away.

faqs.q: When is Prince George's County property tax due?
faqs.a: Bills go out in July and are due in full on September 30. If your home is marked Principal Residence, you can pay half on September 30 and half on December 31.

faqs.q: Where is the Prince George's County Treasury Division?
faqs.a: Go to the customer counter in Largo, 1301 McCormick Drive, Suite 1100, MD 20774, on a weekday. Hours are 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., and 301-952-4030 reaches Customer Service.

faqs.q: Can I pay Prince George's County property tax with cash?
faqs.a: Not at the counter. In person the county takes checks, money orders and cashier's checks, and online you can use cards or e-checks for a fee.

faqs.q: When does the Prince George's County tax sale happen?
faqs.a: Each year on the second Monday in May. Unpaid taxes go to the highest bidder, so ask Treasury for a payoff before that day.

faqs.q: How high is the county transfer tax?
faqs.a: 1.4% for the county, plus recordation at $2.75 per $500 in the 2026 staff table. The state also adds a 0.5% transfer tax, so ask the title company for the total.
